claim: No real assignment violates the explicit linear-polynomial product coefficient convolution.
Grouping equal formal exponential bases commutes with exact coefficient addition.
The polynomial exponent sum (x^2+2x)+(-2x) equals x^2 for every real x.
Dropping the constant shift merges distinct polynomial exponent keys: x^2 and x^2+1.
One shared theta cannot simultaneously equal 1/3 and 2/3.
Independent theta_1 and theta_2 can fit the incompatible rows separately.
A strict positive domain excludes the algebraic boundary theta=0.
Replacing strict positivity with nonnegativity admits the excluded boundary.
The nonzero polynomial x vanishes at one point; that point is no polynomial identity certificate.
The same polynomial has an exact nonzero rational witness inside the open interval (0,1).
With d nonzero, the multiplication graph z*d=n agrees with the division graph z=n/d.
Omitting d nonzero admits arbitrary z at n=d=0, although the intended partial division is undefined.
The nonzero polynomial x-y vanishes on the constrained surface x=y; this is no ambient open-domain identity.
If |rhat-r|<=delta/4 and rhat>=-delta/2 with delta>0, then r>=-delta.
If |rhat-r|<=delta/4 and rhat<-delta/2 with delta>0, then r<0.
The approximate positive branch does not imply unweakened r>=0; a slack countermodel is rhat=-1/2,r=-3/4,delta=1.
